text:
mia: thinking out loud — can we add a tiny \"Quick Inspect\" button on the request row in Console that pulls the sampled req/res for SLA/bug triage? would be handy for SEs and oncall.

sam: love the idea. main concern: PII scope. quick inspect must respect inspect-consent and not surface PHI unless explicit opt-in.

leo: agree. also quota/ttl: button should fetch from the encrypted inspect store, and the preview should expire after 5m. no full unmask in UI.

anya: UX note — make it clear when the sample is live vs cached. maybe a small badge: `sampled · ttl 4m`. and hover explains what data is redacted.

mia: implementation sketch: when button clicked we call internal `GET /v1/inspects/{sample_id}?view=console_preview` and console uses feature-flag `console.quick_inspect_v1`. backend checks route-level consent and tenant opt-in.

sam: pseudo-config idea:
```json
{
  \"quick_inspect\": {
    \"enabled\": true,
    \"max_ttl_seconds\": 300,
    \"allowed_data_classes\": [\"PII_HASHED\", \"ROUTE_METADATA\"]
  }
}
```

leo: We need audit trail. Every inspect view should emit an audit event with actor, sample_id, redaction_profile, and whether data was re-identified (should be false most times). store events in `audit-inspects` topic.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] staged rollout created: feature-flag `console.quick_inspect_v1` -> 10% -> tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

anya: Routing question — if the original request was routed to fallback model due to capacity, the inspect should indicate model variant and route policy used. engineers rely on that to debug quality regressions.

mia: good call. include `served_model` and `route_reason` in metadata, but keep them minimal strings. no raw model weights or logs.

sam: Telemetry: increment `console.quick_inspect.requested` and `console.quick_inspect.allowed` / `denied` with labels: tenant_id, route, redaction_profile. sample rate for telemetry should be 1% by default to avoid high cardinality.

leo: Also add a backend guard: if tenant has high QPS and inspect-store backlog > 100k, deny new quick-inspect reads and return 429 with a friendly UI message.

anya: edge-case: admin support flows. we should allow temporary \"support-unmask\" with legal consent + JIRA link. require an approver and TTL of <24h. store approval event in audit.

mia: implementation tasks: 1) backend API + consent checks, 2) inspect-store TTL enforcement, 3) telemetry dims + sampling, 4) console button + badge + friendly error states, 5) audit events pipeline, 6) feature-flag rollout.

sam: prioritize backend consent and audit first. UI can be toggled off until that lands.

leo: I'll take the backend API + quota guard. sam can own telemetry dims. anya can prototype UI copy. mia will coordinate rollout plan and docs.

mia: assigning: leo -> #issue 5123, sam -> #issue 5124, anya -> #issue 5125, mia -> #issue 5126 for rollout runbook.

ops-bot: [reminder] weekly privacy sync: Thu 16:00 — proposed discussion item: quick-inspect rollout checklist.

mia: thanks all. leaving this open for any privacy/legal wins/concerns. if no blockers by EOD Friday we'll unfreeze the flag for canary. :thumbsup:

sam: pinging @privacy-team for final signoff.

anya: leaving a mockup in the thread: https://share.redwood/mockups/quick-inspect-button (contains alt text only).

leo: one small ask — put a rate limit on per-user quick-inspects (e.g., 30/min) to avoid console-driven scrapers.

mia: yep, add per-user quota to the API layer. thanks!
